purpose: determine whether a PostgreSQL-native read-only adjacency primitive can be built, installed, removed, and executed over the existing edge indexes on PostgreSQL 17 and 18 with exact snapshot behavior and enough raw-read headroom to justify a separately frozen traversal candidate roster

predecessor.reason: The duplicate adjacency relation was terminally not advanced because it nearly doubled storage, doubled or tripled structural-write WAL, and caused two-to-four orders of magnitude destructive-write latency regressions. This successor must not maintain a graph copy.

architecture.execution_boundary: a PostgreSQL backend-local PGXS extension using matched-major relation, relcache, and covering-index scan APIs under GetActiveSnapshot()
architecture.diagnostic_function: p5_native_feasibility.p5_native_adjacency_scan_v1(graph_id int4, anchor_id int8, edge_kind_ids int2[], inbound bool)
architecture.source_storage: public.edge and its existing graph partitions and direction-specific covering indexes
architecture.state_contract: no graph-proportional relation, index, trigger, mutation hook, background worker, shared-memory allocation, mutation epoch, or application-side service
architecture.cache_contract: the feasibility function is called only by its capture runner; Cypher translation and cypherTranslationCacheKey remain unchanged
allowed_scope: one opt-in extension package with one diagnostic schema and one read-only function that always returns one bounded result-and-telemetry row
one backend-native covering-index scan over the resolved graph edge partition per invocation
capture-only exactness, snapshot, lifecycle, resource, and raw-read measurements
forbidden_scope: a shortest-path, all-shortest-path, or ordinary-expansion executor
a selector, fallback policy, promotion manifest, or cache-key change

delivery_matrix.artifact_rule: build a distinct shared library from the same clean source archive with pg_config and server headers matching each PostgreSQL major; never load one major's artifact into the other
required_package_files: C source with an explicit PG_MODULE_MAGIC boundary
required_lifecycle: install files into an isolated matched-major image
stop_conditions: either required major cannot build with warnings treated as errors
either artifact fails CREATE EXTENSION, smoke execution, DROP EXTENSION, or reinstall
the extension requires shared_preload_libraries, superuser execution after installation, an unsafe search_path, a cross-major binary, or an unvalidated relation or index OID
the extension creates or depends on graph-proportional database objects

probe_contract.comparison_contract: the timed native and direct-SQL arms each return one row containing parallel bounded arrays without ORDER BY; the capture runner canonicalizes copied edge/next/kind triples by kind_id and edge_id only after timing before exact comparison
probe_contract.overflow_contract: the native and direct-SQL probes stop at the immutable 4096-row cap plus one sentinel; the capture runner compares the complete bounded sequence and records overflow but no Cypher consumer may observe it
probe_contract.relation_reference: resolve the exact public.edge child whose list-partition bound equals graph_id, then validate its inherited outbound or inbound covering index before opening either OID
probe_contract.index_contract: use the start_id-kind_id or end_id-kind_id inherited covering index, constrain the physical anchor, filter wildcard or requested kinds, obtain edge_id plus the opposite endpoint from the covering tuple when MVCC visibility permits, and report every required heap fetch
probe_contract.interrupt_contract: check interrupts while materializing returned tuples so cancellation is prompt and the same pooled backend can be reused after rollback
probe_contract.snapshot_contract: the native and direct-SQL probes execute on the same connection under Repeatable Read; a concurrent writer test proves that both retain the pre-writer snapshot until transaction end

capture_design.arm_order: four SQL/native blocks and four native/SQL blocks in doubled-Williams order
capture_design.aa_design: a separately captured direct-SQL/direct-SQL order-balanced A/A artifact on each server major
capture_design.source_requirements: clean committed source, checksummed source archive, protocol, extension source, per-major binaries, capture runner, fixtures, and sanitized environment

resource_budgets.catalog_boundary: one extension row, one owned schema, one function, and no dependency from normal DAWGS schema objects

raw_read_gates.high_degree_target_rule: at least one non-overflowing typed or wildcard case on each server major must clear the ratio or absolute-saving alternative after applying that host's A/A floor

pass_authorizes: a separately named and frozen tool-only native traversal candidate roster
a prospective power study calibrated only from this successor's open feasibility traces
pass_does_not_authorize: normal schema installation or a required database extension
reuse of adjacency-materialization evidence as native-extension evidence
next_authorization.failure: terminally stop P5-NATIVE-ADJACENCY-SCAN-V1 without weakening the delivery, resource, or raw-read gates; any retry requires a distinct architecture and protocol identity
